elements.label: Figure 1.12
elements.description:
Chart type: stacked bar chart with six regional panels, each showing years 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018 and 2020. Y-axis: 'Population (in millions)', scale 0 to 25 in steps of 5. Series (bottom to top): Extreme poor (teal), Moderate poor (orange), Economically vulnerable (grey), Economically secure (yellow), Middle-class (blue). No values are printed on the bars; approximate totals (~, in millions) read from the chart:
- Midlands & Northern Mountains: 2010 ~12.7; 2012 ~13.4; 2014 ~13.1; 2016 ~14.2; 2018 ~15.3; 2020 ~12.7. Extreme poor is largest in 2010 (~1.7) and falls to under ~0.5 by 2020; the economically secure segment is the largest part throughout.
- Red River Delta: 2010 ~19.2; 2012 ~19.0; 2014 ~20.4; 2016 ~20.6; 2018 ~21.5; 2020 ~24.0. The middle-class segment grows from ~3 (2010) to ~7 (2020); economically secure is the largest block in all years; extreme poor is near zero.
- Central Highlands: 2010 ~5.2; 2012 ~5.1; 2014 ~5.5; 2016 ~6.0; 2018 ~6.3; 2020 ~5.9. Economically secure and vulnerable are the main segments; extreme poor and middle class are small.
- Northern & Central Region: 2010 ~17.6; 2012 ~18.2; 2014 ~17.9; 2016 ~18.7; 2018 ~20.2; 2020 ~20.3. Economically vulnerable is large in 2010 (~6.5) and shrinks to ~3.7 by 2020; economically secure grows to ~12 by 2020.
- Southeastern area: 2010 ~15.1; 2012 ~16.0; 2014 ~17.4; 2016 ~16.7; 2018 ~17.0; 2020 ~17.4. Middle-class segment rises from near zero to ~8 in 2020, while the economically secure segment falls.
- Mekong River Delta: 2010 ~16.3; 2012 ~17.4; 2014 ~17.4; 2016 ~16.7; 2018 ~16.4; 2020 ~17.0. Economically secure is the largest segment and economically vulnerable is large in 2010 (~5.5) and falls over time; the middle-class segment stays small.
Overall pattern: the number of people in the poor and vulnerable categories falls over time while the economically secure and middle-class segments grow, most strongly in the Red River Delta and Southeastern area.
Source line below the chart: 'Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010–2020.'

| Economically vulnerable | ($3.2-$5.5) | 1,055 – 1,813 | Between the World Bank's LMIC and UMIC poverty lines |
| Economically secure | ($5.5-$15) | 1,813 – 4,946 | Above the World Bank UMIC poverty line, but not yet middle class (see below). |
